% A deliberately hostile document.
%
% Every construct here is one that a LaTeX parser can plausibly get wrong,
% chosen so that getting it wrong is *visible*: a swallowed comment, a
% miscounted brace, a `&` taken for a cell separator when it is inside
% \text{}, a \verb span reflowed across a newline. It is valid LaTeX and
% compiles; anything the editor does to it that stops it compiling, or that
% changes what it prints, is a bug.
%
% Kept as one file rather than split so that a single fixed-point check
% exercises the interactions — a \verb inside a table cell inside a float
% is where the individually-correct rules disagree.

\documentclass[11pt,twoside]{article}

\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm,mathtools}
\usepackage{booktabs,multirow,array}
\usepackage{enumitem}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\usepackage{listings}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\usepackage[capitalise,noabbrev]{cleveref}

% A comment that mentions \begin{document} and } and $ — none of which
% should be read as markup.
\newcommand{\pair}[2]{\ensuremath{\langle #1, #2 \rangle}}
\newcommand{\opt}[2][default]{[#1]\,#2}
\renewcommand{\labelitemi}{$\triangleright$}
\newcommand{\braced}{\{\}}

\makeatletter
\newcommand{\internal@thing}{internal}
\makeatother

\theoremstyle{plain}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\theoremstyle{definition}
\newtheorem{defn}[theorem]{Definition}

\title{Torture: \texorpdfstring{$\alpha$}{alpha}, braces \{like this\}, and 100\% coverage}
\author{A. Tester}
\date{2026-07-27}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section[Short form]{A heading with \emph{markup}, math $\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i$, and braces \{x\}}
\label{sec:first}

Special characters, all escaped: \$ \& \% \# \_ \{ \} \textbackslash{} and a
tilde \~{} and a caret \^{}.

A comment at the end of a line joins the next word without a space,% like this
which is why this sentence has no gap before ``which''.

Inline verbatim with a brace: \verb|if (x) { return } | and with a different
delimiter: \verb+a|b+ and a starred one: \verb*!spaces   kept!.

The macro \pair{a}{b} takes two arguments; \opt{x} takes an optional one and
\opt[explicit]{y} supplies it.

\subsection{Lists that nest}

\begin{itemize}
  \item First, with a trailing comment% not part of the item
  \item Second, containing a nested list:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item inner one
    \item inner two, with an explicit marker below
  \end{enumerate}
  \item[!] A custom marker.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Mathematics}

Inline maths in prose: $\pair{u}{v} \leq \|u\|\,\|v\|$ and a lone
dollar-escaped \$ sign.

\begin{equation}\label{eq:cases}
  f(x) =
  \begin{cases}
    x^2 & \text{if } x \geq 0, \\
    -x  & \text{otherwise.}
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}

An aligned block where the `\&' below is alignment and the one inside
\text{} is not:

\begin{align}
  a &= b + c \label{eq:a} \\
  &= d + e \notag \\
  x &\in \{1, 2, 3\} \quad \text{(a set, not a cell \& not a group)}
\end{align}

A display with a stretched delimiter and a dropped right side:
\[
  \left\{ \frac{1}{2}, \frac{3}{4} \right. \qquad
  \left( \sum_{k} a_k \right)^{\!2}
\]

\begin{subequations}\label{eq:group}
  \begin{align}
    p &= q \label{eq:p} \\
    r &= s \label{eq:r}
  \end{align}
\end{subequations}

  \begin{tabular}{@{}l>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3cm}cc@{}}

    Beta  & \verb|&| literal & $3.0$ & \multicolumn{1}{r}{$4.0$} \\[4pt]
    Gamma & \{braced\} & $5.0$ & $6.0$ \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

A tabular nested inside another:

\begin{tabular}{cc}
  \toprule
  outer & \begin{tabular}{c} inner \\ rows \end{tabular} \\
  \bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{lstlisting}[language=Python,caption={Braces \{ and \} in a caption}]
def f(x):
    if x > 0:  # a comment with % and \ and {
        return {"key": x}
    return None
\end{lstlisting}

  A definition whose body has a display:

\begin{theorem}[Main]\label{thm:main}
  Under \Cref{def:one} and \eqref{eq:cases}, the bound in \eqref{eq:a} holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
